Alright, let me think this through for my farm this year.

---

**My thinking**

I've got 220.1 mu — that's a serious operation, not a smallholder plot. Five years in, I've made my share of mistakes and I've been keeping records since year two. My high school background helps; I actually read the extension bulletins and I know how to calculate nitrogen rates from yield targets instead of just going by "what Dad did." But I won't pretend I've got the intuition of the old guys who've farmed these fields for 40 years. I still call my uncle before making big changes.

Spring soybean and millet — that's my system. It's not the wheat-maize monoculture most of Quzhou runs. I picked this combination deliberately: soybean fixes nitrogen and breaks the cereal disease cycle, millet is drought-tolerant so I'm not beholden to pumping groundwater every 10 days like my neighbors on wheat-maize. Water bills add up fast on 220 mu.

**Area allocation.** I'll split roughly 120 mu soybean, 100.1 mu millet. Last year soybean prices held up well — state reserve buying and the feed market in Shijiazhuang keep demand steady. Millet is more volatile, but specialty "Quzhou xiaomi" fetches a premium if the quality is right. I don't want to over-weight millet because the market is thinner. Soybean also conditions the soil for next year's millet block when I rotate.

**Soybean, 120 mu.** Planting late April, targeting April 25–30 window after soil temperature hits 10°C at 5cm. Using Zhonghuang 30 — certified seed, about 25 yuan/mu. Inoculate with rhizobium; that's cheap insurance for nodulation. Base fertilizer only — 3 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, 5 kg K₂O per mu — no topdress because soybean does its own nitrogen work once nodules form. Over-applying N suppresses nodulation, that's a classic rookie mistake I made in year two. Irrigation: one shot at flowering (R1-R2) if July stays dry, maybe a second at pod-fill. Herbicide pre-emergence (acetochlor + metribuzin), then spot-spray for broadleaf weeds if needed. Target yield 200 kg/mu — conservative; I've hit 220 but soil across 120 mu isn't uniform.

**Millet, 100.1 mu.** Planting mid-May, around May 15–20 once soil warms properly. Using Zhangzagu 10 — hybrid, yields better than landraces but costs more (about 30 yuan/mu). Fertilizer: 10 kg N total, split as 7 kg base + 3 kg topdress at jointing. P 5 kg/mu, K 5 kg/mu all at base. Millet is drought-tolerant so I plan zero irrigation unless we get a true drought through July — then one emergency flood. Herbicide is tricky on millet; I'll rely more on mechanical cultivation (small tractor) twice. Watch for corn borer and armyworm. Target 300 kg/mu.

**Labor.** Household is four but only two of us work the farm full time. On 220 mu I absolutely need hired help — planting week, topdressing, and especially harvest. Budget around 70 hired days across the year. I own a 40hp tractor and a planter; I custom-hire a combine for harvest on both crops.

**Costs.** Roughly 450 yuan/mu on soybean × 120 = 54,000; roughly 420 yuan/mu on millet × 100.1 = 42,042. Plus hired labor (~9,000) and custom combine (~11,000). Call it about 116,000 yuan total cash outlay. I can cover most of it from last year's proceeds and a small input loan from the credit cooperative.
